results.title: Integrated Park Module (IPM) Fails to Lock Transmission in Park — Rollaway Risk

issues_found: Repair cost field shows $0-$0 which is technically correct since it's a free recall OTA/dealer software update, but may be worth noting it's a recall remedy rather than out-of-pocket repair
Warranty claim counts (4 Maverick Hybrid, 22 Mach-E, 16 F-150 Lightning) could not be independently verified from search results but the overall recall is confirmed
audit.evidence: NHTSA recall 25V863 / Ford recall 25C69 issued December 12, 2025 covers 272,645 vehicles including 80,468 2025-2026 Ford Maverick Hybrid pickups, where the IPM pawl can bind against the slider, preventing mechanical engagement of Park within 2.9 seconds and violating FMVSS 114. Remedy is a free OTA or dealer software update with interim letters mailed February 2, 2026.

results.title: Connected Touch Radio Rear View Camera Image Freeze (Recall 24S59 / 24V684)

audit.evidence: NHTSA Recall 24V684 / Ford 24S59 confirms the Connected Touch Radio (CTR) software memory issue causing rear-view camera freeze on 2022-2024 Mavericks, affecting 144,516 vehicles built 2/3/2021-11/28/2023, with two crashes reported and no DTCs involved; remedy is a free software update.

results.title: Front Windshield Wiper Motor Failure (Recall 24S51 / NHTSA 24V594)

audit.evidence: NHTSA recall 24V594 / Ford 24S51 is confirmed as a real recall affecting 2023-2024 Ford Maverick (and 2023 Bronco Sport / Mustang Mach-E) for windshield wiper motor failure caused by missing sealer allowing water intrusion. Dealers inspect and replace the motor free of charge, consistent with the $0 repair cost and high severity (safety-related visibility risk) listed.

results.title: 8F35 Transmission Shudder/Buck/Jerk Below 35 mph and Output Carrier Bearing Wear (Early 2022 Builds)

issues_found: TSB 21-2389 explicitly applies to 2019-2021 Edge/Nautilus only, not the Maverick — citing it as carry-over to Maverick is inferential, not a formal Ford position
The more directly applicable bulletin for the output carrier bearing wear is TSB 22-2281 (Transit Connect, builds on/before 20-Dec-2021), which the description omits by name
DTC list is broad/generic; codes like P0727, P0771, P2700, P2701, P2704 are not specifically called out in either TSB and appear over-inclusive for the described shudder/carrier-wear conditions
Year range '2022-2022' is narrower than the affected build window (early 2022 builds before Dec 20, 2021 production cutoff) — phrasing is acceptable but could be more precise
audit.evidence: Ford TSB 21-2389 documents the 8F35 shudder/buck/jerk below 35 mph but is officially scoped to 2019-2021 Edge/Nautilus; a separate TSB 22-2281 covers 8F35 slipping/harsh engagement and output carrier failures on units built on/before 20-Dec-2021, and Maverick owner forums widely report both conditions on early 2022 EcoBoost Mavericks with the 8F35.

results.title: Engine Block Heater May Crack and Cause Underhood Fire When Plugged In (Recall 25SA4 / 25V685)

audit.evidence: NHTSA Campaign 25V685 / Ford Recall 25SA4 confirms the issue for 2022-2024 Ford Maverick (among other models), citing solder-joint cracks in the engine block heater allowing coolant intrusion, salt-bridge formation, short circuit, and underhood fire risk; 46 fire reports as of September 2025, mostly in Canada. Repair is a free replacement once redesigned parts are available, no DTCs are applicable, and severity 'high' is appropriate for a fire-risk recall.

results.title: HPCM Software Forces Vehicle into Neutral While Driving (Recall 24S33 / 24V-330)

audit.evidence: NHTSA recall 24V-330 (Ford 24S33) issued May 3, 2024 covers 2022-2024 Ford Maverick Hybrids with HPCM software that can force neutral while driving, then enter limp mode up to 30 mph; remedy is a free dealer software update. Owner reports confirm the listed DTCs (U1010, U1011, U1028, U0418, U0401, U0131) and the symptom description matches official documentation.
